title: Shared Drop Folder for Notifications
description:
**SITUATION:**

**Notification-service** sends the note a customer sees, a confirmation or a receipt. It does not receive that note over the network. A program writes a file in `/srv/notifications/outbox`, and the service sends that file.

`payment-bot` and `order-bot` are service accounts. Each of those accounts also has a private group of the same name, which is why the receipt's group showed up as `payment-bot`, so `order-bot` could not read it. `payment-bot` writes the receipt. `order-bot` reads it before writing the confirmation. A new file must stay in `notify`.

Root is the owner, not another member of `notify`. An account in `notify` could add a file and, with that same permission, delete someone else's. The folder's group was set to root. `payment-bot` and `order-bot` are in `notify`, so both stopped. Root stays the owner. The group must be `notify`, and accounts may delete only their own file.

Compliance uses the account `auditor` to read what was sent. It must read every message, including later files, and never add or delete one. Keep `auditor` out of `notify`.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Set `/srv/notifications/outbox` so `payment-bot` can add the receipt, `order-bot` can read that receipt and add the confirmation, a new file stays in group `notify`, a bot cannot delete a file it does not own, and anyone outside `notify` cannot list the folder.
2. Let `auditor` read that folder and every file created in it later, without adding `auditor` to `notify` and without letting `auditor` add or delete a message.

**SPEC:**

- `/srv/notifications/outbox` is `root:notify`, mode `3770`
- ACL on that folder: `user:auditor:r-x`
- Default ACL on that folder: `default:user:auditor:r-x`

**REFERENCES:**

- [DevSetu Blog — Users, Groups, and Permissions](/play/devops-engineer/linux/read/users-groups-and-permissions)

hints: You are learner on a real Ubuntu machine with systemd; sudo works without a password.
Reset gives you a fresh machine (your changes are wiped).
Read SPEC carefully, then Submit — the grader checks the machine itself.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Shared Drop Folder for Notifications

Plain `rwx` modes have three limits for shared folders:
- New files get the creator's own group, so teammates can't read them. The **setgid** bit on the directory fixes that.
- Anyone who can write the directory can delete anyone's file. The **sticky** bit fixes that.
- There's only one group slot, so a read-only outsider can't be given access. **ACLs** fix that.

Docs: `man chmod` (SETUID AND SETGID BITS, RESTRICTED DELETION FLAG) · `man setfacl` · `man getfacl`

## Group ownership and special bits

```bash
sudo chgrp notify /srv/notifications/outbox
sudo chmod 3770 /srv/notifications/outbox
ls -ld /srv/notifications/outbox        # drwxrws--T  root notify
```

The leading `3` is `2` (setgid) plus `1` (sticky). In `ls`, an `s` in the group slot means setgid, and a `T`/`t` in the others slot means sticky.

## ACL for the auditor

```bash
sudo setfacl -m u:auditor:rx /srv/notifications/outbox        # access now
sudo setfacl -d -m u:auditor:rx /srv/notifications/outbox     # default: inherited by new files
getfacl /srv/notifications/outbox
ls -ld /srv/notifications/outbox        # a trailing + means an ACL is set
```

## Prove it

```bash
sudo -u payment-bot sh -c 'echo paid > /srv/notifications/outbox/receipt'
ls -l /srv/notifications/outbox/receipt                                # group notify
sudo -u order-bot cat /srv/notifications/outbox/receipt                # order-bot can read the receipt
sudo -u order-bot rm  /srv/notifications/outbox/receipt                # Operation not permitted (sticky)
sudo -u order-bot sh -c 'echo placed > /srv/notifications/outbox/confirm'
sudo -u auditor cat /srv/notifications/outbox/receipt                  # works (ACL)
sudo -u auditor touch /srv/notifications/outbox/a1                     # Permission denied
sudo rm /srv/notifications/outbox/receipt /srv/notifications/outbox/confirm
```

Then **Submit**.
